prompt: Play an interviewer, and help me fix my pronunciation.

muc.title: Talking with your voice
muc.text: Last time, AI read text out loud. Now we put listening and talking together. You ask out loud, and AI answers out loud, like calling a friend. But inside, there are two very different ways to do it.

muc.title: Three machines in a row
muc.text: The old way chains three machines: one transcribes your words into text, AI writes a reply, and a third machine reads it out loud. Each stage takes a moment, so you wait a few seconds in total.

muc.title: Your tone gets lost
muc.text: Worse, once it becomes text, your tone of voice disappears. You say "yeah, fine" in a sad voice, AI only sees those two words, and answers cheerfully.

muc.title: One brain that listens and talks
muc.text: The new way uses one model: it hears the sound directly and speaks sound directly, without turning it into text. It can notice a sad voice or laughter, and answer in a tone that fits you.

muc.title: Answers in about half a second
muc.text: With fewer stages, AI can answer in about half a second, close to the pace of human conversation. You can even interrupt: if you cut in, it stops to listen.

muc.title: A warm voice isn't always right
muc.text: But a natural-sounding voice doesn't mean the information is right. For important things like medicine or money, still double-check.

muc.title: Practice interviews with AI
muc.text: Turn on voice mode and say: "Play an interviewer, and help me fix my pronunciation". The same works for practicing a new language: if you get it wrong, just try again. Nobody's laughing.

muc.title: Next up: watching video
muc.text: Listening and talking, done. Now on to watching a whole video. How does AI watch video? See you in part 4.
